claims.claim_ar: حصر الكلام باستثناء الإذن بعبارة «إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ»، أي تقييد قدرة النطق إلى إذن ربّي
claims.claim_en: Restriction (qasr) signaled by 'illa' in «إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ», limiting speaking so that no soul speaks except by God's permission.

claims.claim_ar: توظيف تصويري لمقام الكلام، حيث يرد في التفسير تشبيه أقوال الكافرين أو الطعن في الحقّ بـ«كلام المجانين» — قراءة مجازية للقول الباطل مقارنة بالكلام الهذياني
claims.claim_en: Figurative/metaphorical reading in the commentary likens certain speech to 'the words of the mad' («فتتكلم بكلام المجانين»). This treats speech (تَكَلَّمَ) in a metaphorical/pejorative sense when applied to falsehood.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted commentary (Zamakhshari) interprets speech as madness in a particular context; applying this reading to the ayah may be interpretive/extrapolative and needs checking against other tafsir or the requested authors.

claims.claim_ar: تقديم اسم الزمان «يوم» في بداية العبارة («يَوْمَ يَأْتِ») لتأكيد واقعته وأهمّيّته (تقديم تأخير لعنصر الزمان)
claims.claim_en: Fronting the temporal noun 'yawm' («يَوْمَ يَأْتِ») places emphasis on the Day itself — a taqdim/takhir (advance/delay) that foregrounds the temporal setting of the event.
claims.needs_review_reason: The available commentary fragment mentions describing the day («وصف اليوم») but does not explicitly analyze word order; the claim is a plausible rhetorical reading but should be verified with fuller stylistic commentary.

warnings: Provided source chunks are limited (primarily excerpts from al-Kashshaf and a parsing note) and do not include the full set of requested authors (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir-balagha) — claims are drawn only from the available fragments.

Some claims (especially the figurative reading of تَكَلَّمُ and the word-order emphasis) are interpretive links between the ayah and the available commentary excerpts; these are marked with 'needs_review' and should be checked against fuller tafsir/balagha treatments.

Source_quote_ar fields are exact substrings from the provided chunks; where the chunk comment applies to analogous language or context rather than this exact ayah, the claim notes that it may be extrapolative.
